elements.note: Counted by reading corpus/elements.md: six headings (h1, two h2 before the break, h3, h4, and the h2 after it), an image and a footnote in the opening paragraph, an ordered list whose second item holds a nested bullet list (2 lists, 4 items), two fenced code blocks, one blockquote, and six paragraphs - five in the body plus the footnote's own. The thematic break is not an element: it carries no content, and every parser here drops it by declared policy.

profile.note: Counted by reading corpus/profile.md: one heading, four body paragraphs (one of which is the embed on its own line), two wikilinks, one embed, two tags, and a callout carrying one paragraph - five paragraphs in total. Mycelium Markdown Profile syntax (D-022), so this family has one route and makes no claim about the others.

retry-policy.note: Counted by reading source.md: two headings, a link in the opening paragraph, a bullet list of two items, a definition list of one term (a list with one item, whose definition is a paragraph), a 2x3 table counted with its header row, one fenced code block, one blockquote, and four paragraphs - the opening one, the one under Backoff, the quotation's body and the definition's body.

text-layer.note: A hand-built single-page PDF whose text layer is five lines with no blank line between them, so a faithful text extractor returns one block. There is no structure in the file to find: a PDF's text layer carries characters and positions, not headings (ADR-0032).

two-pages.note: A hand-built two-page PDF: page one has a text layer (one block, as above), page two has none. The declaration says `opaque` because that is what a faithful parser must produce for a page it cannot read - an element recorded as lost, not a page quietly missing from the output.

deviations.list: CommonMark has no definition lists and the Mycelium Markdown Profile adds none, so markdown-it reads the term and its definition as the one paragraph they look like: the text survives, the list does not exist.
deviations.list_item: CommonMark has no definition lists and the Mycelium Markdown Profile adds none, so markdown-it reads the term and its definition as the one paragraph they look like: the text survives, the list does not exist.

deviations.list: pandoc's DOCX writer renders a definition list as two styled paragraphs, so there is no list in the file for docling to find; the term and its definition arrive as prose.
deviations.list_item: pandoc's DOCX writer renders a definition list as two styled paragraphs, so there is no list in the file for docling to find; the term and its definition arrive as prose.
deviations.paragraph: Same cause as `list`: with the definition list flattened, its term arrives as a paragraph of its own, one more than the source has.
deviations.quote: pandoc renders a blockquote as a styled paragraph in DOCX and as <blockquote> in HTML, and docling's backends emit the content of both as text: the quotation survives without its wrapper.

deviations.list: pandoc's HTML writer renders a definition list as <dl>, which docling reads as a list whose item holds a nested list - one list more than the source has.
deviations.list_item: Same cause as `list`: the definition becomes an item of a nested list rather than a paragraph.
deviations.paragraph: Same cause as `list`: the definition's body is a list item in HTML, so one paragraph fewer.
deviations.quote: pandoc renders a blockquote as a styled paragraph in DOCX and as <blockquote> in HTML, and docling's backends emit the content of both as text: the quotation survives without its wrapper.

policies: definition lists became lists; the term/definition roles are lost
PDF text layer only: no headings, tables or reading-order analysis (ADR-0032, and ADR-0040 for what the alternative was measured to cost)

deviations.footnote: CommonMark has no footnotes and the Mycelium Markdown Profile adds none, so markdown-it reads the definition line as the paragraph it looks like: the note's text survives, its role does not.

deviations.code_block: pandoc's DOCX writer emits both fenced blocks as consecutive SourceCode paragraphs, and docling joins a run of them into one code item; the text of both survives inside it.
deviations.footnote: docling's DOCX backend does not read word/footnotes.xml, so the note's body never reaches the KIR at all (BUG-0016).
deviations.opaque: The other half of `footnote`: the adapter counts the notes the container declares and records each one docling did not surface as an opaque `lost` element, so the loss is counted by the fidelity report instead of being invisible (BUG-0016).
